messages:
priya: Hey team — Acme is hitting a 400 from our /v1/rerank endpoint when they include a top-level `query` and also have a `query` field inside candidate objects. They say this started after a data pipeline change.
emily: Can you paste the payload and the exact error body?
priya: Pasting a minimized repro they sent:
```
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "query": "how to reset password",
  "candidates": [
    { "id": "c1", "query": "reset steps", "text": "Step 1..." },
    { "id": "c2", "query": "password help", "text": "Step 2..." }
  ]
}
```
Response: 400 Bad Request
```
{ "error": "invalid_request", "message": "ambiguous field 'query' found in payload" }
```
rolf: Huh. We normally expect `query` as the user query top-level. Looks like our parser flattens nested keys and raises on duplicate names. Did they try moving candidate-level `query` under `metadata` or renaming it?
priya: They said renaming candidate field to `candidate_query` fixed it, but they need a migration path. Ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/34721
eng-oncall: This matches a known ambiguity in the rerank input parser: if a nested object contains a field with the same name as a top-level reserved key we trigger a generic 400. Workaround is to avoid reserved keys inside candidates (use `metadata` or different name). We should return a clearer 4xx explaining the conflicting path.
emily: Is there any chance this is related to candidate count or size? Any other errors in logs?
priya: Customer also sent one run where candidates=1200 and we returned 422 on that attempt (we enforce a 1000 candidate limit by default). So they hit both issues: over-limit + ambiguous field in another run.
support-bot: :warning: Customer Acme (acct: acme-inc) SLA: Standard. Impact: blocking a migration. Please prioritize.
rolf: Proposed fix: validate candidate objects server-side and if a nested key name collides with a reserved top-level key return `400` with message: "conflicting field 'query' in candidates[i]; rename or move into candidates[i].metadata". Also add a linter in our docs/examples calling out common reserved keys like `query`, `collection`, `id`, `text`.
eng-oncall: Agree. Also add a telemetry flag to count how many requests hit this ambiguity so we can prioritize. Who owns the patch? eng-runtime + api-validation.
emily: Action items: (1) priya to attach full customer repro and logs to ticket 34721, (2) rolf to draft validation message and PR, (3) eng-oncall to add telemetry/alert, (4) support to notify customer ETA. I'll follow up in this thread once we have a PR.
priya: Uploaded logs and repro to the ticket. Noted.
eng-oncall: If anyone wants a quick local repro I can share a small harness that mimics our JSON schema parser.
emily: Thanks everyone. Marking this P1 for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
